steps.text: Place olive oil, lime juice, onion, tarragon, 1 teaspoon salt, and hot sauce in a large, resealable plastic bag; shake to combine. Add chicken thighs, coat with marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil grate.
Remove chicken from marinade and shake off excess. Discard remaining marinade. Season chicken with salt and black pepper.
Cook on the preheated grill until no longer pink in the center, about 30 minutes. (Chicken thighs don't dry out easily, so don't be afraid to cook them a bit longer if needed.)

raw_recipe.headline: Lime-Tarragon Grilled Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This lime-tarragon grilled chicken recipe starts with a lime-tarragon marinade with hot sauce for juicy, flavorful, moist, and delicious grilled chicken.

video.description: Lime is a refreshing marinade that makes the chicken juicy and delicious. Marinate overnight for extra flavorful chicken. Hot sauce adds some spice while the tarragon perfectly pairs with meat. Serve with potato salad during an outdoor party!

review.reviewBody: The whole family enjoyed this recipe. I combined everything in a freezer bag and froze it. When I was ready to grill, I removed it from the freezer the night before to thaw. I added some of the juice from the marinade to my rice cooker for a flavorful rice dish.

This was delicious! I adapted it for the oven, because I'm a busy student and didn't have time to do grilling. I put it in the oven at 400 degrees Fahrenheit for 40 minutes and it came out perfect. I also added carrots, potatoes, and broccoli, which I tossed in some of the marinade. I didn't want to cut into a big onion for 2 TBSP worth, so I cut up the white parts of 2 green onions for the marinade and used the green parts for garnishing (I wish I'd also saved some lime for garnishing). This recipe has a really nice, zesty, interesting flavor profile and is perfect if you want an easy and different chicken dish and you're getting tired of ones with garlic. Thanks for the recipe Ms. Betancourt!

This is a nice recipe and the chicken was certainly moist and tasty. In my case, however, the flavors I was expecting did not exactly come through. I had more chicken thighs than the recipe called for so I needed to adjust measurements. One effect was the heat really did not come through. This part was tricky so perhaps need to recalculate. I also did not have tarragon so I did my best to substitute other suitable herbs. The substitutions may not have been up to the task. I am eager to try this again at some point. 

I will say that this recipe is a great suggestion for cooking chicken thighs. They take the heat of the grill well, and they are hard to dry out. Do not use chicken breasts as it is not the same. When grilling place the thighs skin side down over direct heat for 3-5 minutes. You want a nice char of the skin. After that turn chicken over and move to indirect heat for 30-35 minutes. Cover the grill with vents partially open and leave the chicken alone so the heat can do its work. When cooking over indirect heat it is helpful to have a drip pan of some sort to catch any juices.

I added some chopped garlic and chives to the marinade. Then I upped the oil and lime juice to 3/4 cup each and added some marinade to the rice pilaf. I've made it on the stove when weather wasn't nice. Instead of adding marinade to the rice, I added mushrooms to the saute pan and then added marinade to made a sauce. Mmmmmm good!

Too bland as written. I changed the tarragon to fresh and used 1 ounce, then added 1 teaspoon of anise seed to enhance the taste of licorice; instead of hot sauce I added 6 drops of Tijuana Flats "Smack my and call me Sally", then added 1 tablespoon of agave nectar. Plus, I decreased the amount of oil. Tasted the marinade and it crossed the entire palate; let you know how it grills.
Cut olive oil in half and add 1/4 C. Tarragon vinegar. Cut salt completely. Will make again with poss some more modifications.

Liked the just right tang from the lime juice. I used canola oil instead of olive oil (didn’t have enough olive oil on hand at the time) and substituted ½ teaspoons of fresh tarragon for the dried. The chicken pieces marinated overnight.

I used boneless, skinless chicken thighs and I did not use hot sauce as we do not like spicy food. These are the only differences I made to this recipe. It was easy to make and we loved the flavors. I intend to make it again this weekend when I have house guests. I'm sure they will love it too.

I make this at least once a week as part of my food prep for the week. By far the best marinade I have found. I use the broiler as I have no grill. 15 minutes to juicy flavorful chicken for the whole week. Goes with everything; in salads, wraps or main dish!!
This was great for chicken kabobs. I used half the amount of olive oil, 1 Tbsp. of dried minced onion, Frank's red hot, and let this marinate 24 hours.

I really like this recipe. Small suggestions, use coarse salt and pepper and use generously to the chicken directly, double the hot sauce or don't bother. If you don't marinate in a ziplock, do that, way more effective than just using a dish. I love the salt and lime and Tarragon together. It's a great flavor combo. I do really suggest the coarse salt for both flavor and texture.
A great marinade for chicken thighs. I didn't change a thing. Nice recipe.
Delicious, tender juicy chicken. Substituted margoram for tarragon only because I was out of tarragon.
Good
Made as is, delicious!
It was good. I used fresh tarragon and wish I had used a lot more. I think this would be a great marinade for lamb.
Best grilled chicken ever.
It was okay baked. Too much lime favor. I will cut it back the next time I make it.

Made almost as written (omitted the hot sauce) and the chicken was very good--moist/tender! I wanted more tarragon or a little less lime; hubs thought it was a perfect meld of flavors. Overall, we enjoyed the flavor of the chicken very much. Glad I tried this recipe, definitely a keeper and will make again!. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
I should have let it marinate longer. Would add more hot sauce but overall great recipe!
